approach: Measure first, then cut. The one cost I found in code: `run_check` in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs polls `child.try_wait()` and then sleeps a fixed 200 ms. A fast check (the fixtures' `sh -c grep…` checks) almost never exits before the first poll, so every check run pays about 200 ms, and each lifecycle/job_plan/retry/steward/drain job runs several checks. Change the poll to start at 2 ms and double up to the existing 200 ms cap. The cap, the deadline and the kill-switch logic stay as they are. Then time each of the five binaries with `cargo test --locked --test <name>` before and after (the producer's own machine), profile what remains (fixture git init/commit per test, process spawns, drain's sleeping fakes) and cut only what profiling shows: build a template fixture repo once per binary (copy it or `git clone --local` instead of init+config+add+commit), and drop needless git calls in common/mod.rs. Record measured results and the cause per binary in docs/decisions.md, and add a CHANGELOG entry. No test is removed or weakened.

decisions.choice: Backoff poll (2 ms doubling to the 200 ms cap) in run_check
decisions.reason: The fixed 200 ms sleep is the one unconditional per-check delay I saw in code; backoff removes it for fast checks and keeps the same cap and timeout for slow ones, so timeout and kill-switch tests still behave.

rejected.option: Add a poll-interval field to CheckContext, set short only in tests
rejected.why: Needs edits at 2 run.rs sites and 5 checks.rs test sites, and the tests would need a hook through Athena; larger for the same gain.

rejected.option: Leave checks.rs alone and only change test fixtures
rejected.why: Cannot remove a delay that lives in production code that every fixture job runs.

rejected.option: Block on child.wait() in a helper thread
rejected.why: A bigger change to deadline and kill handling than the request needs.

decisions.choice: Build the fixture repository once per test binary and copy it per test, only if profiling shows git setup matters
decisions.reason: Fixture::with_config runs git init, four config calls, add and commit for every test; a template copy keeps each test isolated while doing the work once.

rejected.option: Share one mutable repository between tests
rejected.why: Tests mutate it and run in parallel; it would make them flaky and weaken isolation.

rejected.option: Adopt cargo-nextest, sccache or a shared target dir
rejected.why: Out of scope. The user rejected nextest (584 s vs 673 s, about 13%, brain-measured); sccache (D79) and a shared target dir are recorded as considered alternatives only.

decisions.choice: Report only numbers measured in the job in docs/decisions.md; the 67 s compile / 673 s run split and nextest figures are labeled brain-measured
decisions.reason: The evidence rule: every number is measured or labeled.

rejected.option: Estimate times for binaries not re-timed

steps: Record a baseline: `cargo test --locked --no-run`, then time each of `--test lifecycle|job_plan|drain|retry|steward` separately and the total test count (`cargo test --locked` summary).

Profile the slowest tests in each binary (`-- --report-time` is unstable, so use per-test timing from running with `--test-threads=1` and a wall-clock timer, or a temporary timer in the helper) to see whether setup, checks or sleeps dominate.
Implement the backoff in checks.rs run_check; keep the cap, deadline and kill-switch code.
Cut the remaining costs found: template fixture in common/mod.rs, trimmed setup in the five test files, and shorter fake waits where no assertion depends on them. Touch run.rs only if it is needed.

risks.risk: Faster polling lets timing-dependent tests race, for example a kill-switch test that expects a check to still be running.
risks.mitigation: Run each affected binary several times and the full suite twice; fix any flake by changing the test's synchronization without weakening assertions.

risks.risk: The fixture template copy changes test isolation or git state such as hooks and config.
risks.mitigation: Copy the whole tree including .git into a fresh tempdir per test, and keep the same config and commit message.
Report the measured result honestly in the decision and the CHANGELOG, with the remaining cost by binary.

demonstrations.method: Read the new decision in the diff and compare its numbers with the producer's reported timings.
demonstrations.observes: A new decision with before/after seconds labeled measured for lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry and steward, and a cause per binary.

Compile 67 s vs run 673 s on 4 cores labeled brain-measured; nextest 0.9.148 (584 s vs 673 s, about 13%) listed as rejected with that reason; sccache per D79 and a shared target dir listed as considered; no other unmeasured number.

demonstrations.observes: No athena.toml, ci.yml or tool pin changed; CHANGELOG.md has an entry; no #[test] removed or #[ignore] added; assertions are unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of checks.rs, run.rs and the tests.
demonstrations.observes: Only the poll backoff (the 200 ms cap unchanged) and fixture/test changes; no default config or timeout value changed.

demonstrations.method: Run the full suite and read the totals.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass with none ignored; the timeout and kill-switch tests in checks.rs still pass, so a failing or slow check still fails the run. Wall time is the producer's report; the verifier confirms only the passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the backoff broke deadline or kill handling, the checks.rs timeout tests (300 ms deadline on `sleep 30`) would fail; if a test were dropped, the total count would fall.

demonstrations.observes: Both exit 0 with no warnings or diffs.
demonstrations.fails_without: Unformatted or lint-warning code would make them fail.

open_questions: checks.rs is not on the deliverable list but holds the 200 ms poll; the backoff keeps the 200 ms cap, but a strict reading of 'production defaults unchanged' may object. If so, add a test-only interval instead.
